Issues.Title: fix(forms): resync select when the text of an option without a value changes
Issues.Body: ## PR Checklist Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements: - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type What kind of change does this PR introduce? - [x] Bugfix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? In Signal Forms, a change of an option's text (`{{ label() }}`) does not inform the select control, not even when the option has no `value` attribute and the text is its value. ```html ``` In B the select stays empty after `label.set('two')`, although the option now matches the field value. Issue Number: #71443 ## What is the new behavior? In B a text change now informs the select control: it selects the option once the text matches the field value, and shows nothing when the text no longer matches. A is unchanged, because with a `value` attribute the text is not the value of the option. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [ ] Yes - [x] No ## Other information I followed the review in #71444: - A text change is only relevant when the parent of the changed text node is an `` is not handled; but we can cover this case as well (`closest('option')`) if preferred - I added the two requested tests and a third one: 1. text changes away from the field value 2. an option with an explicit value) 3. one test for the text changing to the field value I also updated the doc comments in `select.ts` (the first one was stale, the second one missed the `@param`/`@returns` tags) and declares a return type of boolean.

Issues.Title: animate.enter and (animate.enter) replay enter animations on already-rendered DOM during SSR client hydration
Issues.Body:
When an SSR application uses `provideClientHydration()`, elements and component hosts (including bootstrapped roots and hydrated `<router-outlet>` components) that were already rendered in the server HTML and reused in place during client hydration still trigger `animate.enter` (and `(animate.enter)` callbacks) on bootstrap, causing visible flash/re-entry animations on static SSR content (and similarly when `@defer (hydrate on ...)` blocks incrementally hydrate).

Before submitting a fix (cc @jessicajaniuk @alxhub), could we confirm the intended semantics on two edge cases:
1. Should `(animate.enter)` JS callbacks be suppressed alongside `animate.enter` class bindings on hydrated nodes (since `(animate.enter)`'s `animationComplete()` is a no-op and third-party WAAPI/GSAP callbacks otherwise replay the same flash on hydrated DOM, while subsequent client-side insertions like `@if`/`@for`/router navigations still fire both)?
2. For `ngSkipHydration` components, where Angular reuses the host element itself but clears and re-creates its subtree from scratch on the client, should `animate.enter` be skipped on the reused host element while still running on the newly client-rendered children inside the skipped subtree?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "animate.enter and (animate.enter) replay enter animations on already-rendered DOM during SSR client hydration" (#72146)

Issues.Title: fix(core): release leavingNodes when animate.leave resolves to no classes
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When an element with an `[animate.leave]` binding is detached, `node_manipulation` eagerly calls `trackLeavingNodes(tNode, rNode, parentLView)`. If `runLeaveAnimations` subsequently resolves an empty class list (`''`, `'   '`, `[]`, `null`, `undefined`), it pushes a resolver onto `LView`'s leave animation entry, adds `lView[ID]` to `allLeavingAnimations`, and immediately calls `resolve()` without running `animateLeaveClassRunner`.

Because `clearLeavingNodes` is only called by `animateLeaveClassRunner` and `leaveAnimationFunctionCleanup`, the `{el, declarationView}` entry remains retained in the module-level `leavingNodes` `WeakMap` for the lifetime of the `TNode`, leaking every detached element and its declaration view. A similar leak also occurred if `injector.get(ANIMATION_QUEUE)` threw (e.g. during `ApplicationRef` teardown) after `trackLeavingNodes` had already been called.

Issue Number: #72141

## What is the new behavior?

- In `runLeaveAnimations`, only push to `resolvers` and add `lView[ID]` to `allLeavingAnimations` when `activeClasses` is non-empty.
- In `node_animations` (inside the tree-shaken animation runtime), clear the tracked `leavingNodes` entry for `(tNode, rNode)` once leave animations settle or when the animation queue cannot be resolved / no animations run. Clearing at settlement rather than inside `runLeaveAnimations`'s empty-class branch preserves `leavingNodes` tracking and `declarationView` when an empty `[animate.leave]` is composed with an active `animate.leave` on the same element or when a descendant has an active leave animation.
- In `cancelLeavingNodes`, delete the `tNode` entry from `leavingNodes` once its array becomes empty.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Fixes #72141

Issues.Title: docs(core): correct forwardRef usage in standalone example
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines.
- [ ] Tests for the changes have been added (documentation-only change; no tests required).
- [x] Docs have been added / updated.

## PR Type

- [x] Documentation content changes

## What is the current behavior?

The `Circle standalone reference import example` uses `forwardRef` on `ChildComponent` to reference `ParentComponent`.

However, `ParentComponent` is declared before `ChildComponent`, so the reference to `ParentComponent` is already available when the `ChildComponent` decorator is evaluated.

At the same time, `ChildComponent` is referenced in the `ParentComponent` decorator before its declaration, which requires `forwardRef`.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

Move `forwardRef` to the `ParentComponent` imports to defer the reference to `ChildComponent`, which has not yet been declared.

Use a direct reference to `ParentComponent` in the `ChildComponent` imports, since it has already been declared.

This makes the example consistent with the declaration order of the components and correctly demonstrates the use of `forwardRef` in circular standalone component imports.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Same aplies to https://angular.dev/api/core/forwardRef

Issues.Title: fix(core): update standalone directiveDefs and pipeDefs during HMR
Issues.Body:
In `mergeWithExistingDefinition`, `directiveDefs` and `pipeDefs` were always restored from `clone` to preserve remote scopes patched by `ɵɵsetComponentScope` from an `NgModule` file, which does not re-run during HMR of the component file.

Standalone components never use `ɵɵsetComponentScope` because their imports are inlined directly onto the component definition (in `ngtsc`, `handler.ts` keeps non-self dependencies during HMR and emits the component self-reference only while used in the template). Always restoring `clone` left removed standalone directives active, caused swapped or newly added standalone directives to fail silently and pipes to throw `NG0302`, and broke recursive self-references.

Use `newDef.directiveDefs` and `newDef.pipeDefs` directly for standalone components (including `null`), while keeping `clone.directiveDefs` and `clone.pipeDefs` unconditionally for non-standalone components. Add DOM-level acceptance specs in `hmr_spec.ts`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(core): update standalone directiveDefs and pipeDefs during HMR" (#72126)

Issues.Title: feat(forms): support binding numeric values to `<select>` in signal forms
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Native `<select [formField]="...">` elements in Signal Forms only accept `string` models. Attempting to bind a `number` or `number | null` model fails template type-checking, and the runtime reads/writes `<select>` values strictly as strings (including inside the `MutationObserver` re-sync callback).

Issue Number: Refs #68217

## What is the new behavior?

Native single-select `<select [formField]="...">` elements now support binding either `string` subtypes (string, string literal unions, string enums, `T extends string`) **or** `number | null` subtypes (`number`, `number | null`, numeric literal unions, numeric enums, `T extends number | null`):

- **Template type-checking (`TcbNativeFieldOp`)**: checks the field's value signal against `(() => string) | (() => number | null)`.
  - Covariant `(() => string)` preserves full backwards compatibility with existing string literal unions, string enums, and generic string-constrained fields.
  - Covariant `(() => number | null)` supports non-nullable `number`, `number | null`, numeric literal unions, and numeric enums.
  - Because function return types do not distribute across the union, mixed models (`string | null`, `string | number`, `string | number | null`) are strictly rejected at compile time, keeping `null` unambiguous at runtime.
- **Runtime (`native.ts` & `control_native.ts`)**:
  - Uses `isSelect(element) && !element.multiple` (works in both browsers and Domino/SSR, where `HTMLSelectElement.type` is `undefined`).
  - `getNativeControlValue`: if the current model value is `number` or `null`, parses `''` as `null`, valid numeric strings via `Number(...)`, and non-numeric or whitespace-only values as `NativeInputParseError`. `string` models continue to return `element.value` unchanged.
  - `setNativeControlValue`: writes numeric values via `String(value)` and converts `NaN` and `null` to `''`.
  - `observeSelectMutations`: re-syncs via `setNativeControlValue(...)` so dynamically added `<option>` elements properly select numeric, `null`, and `NaN` values.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

All existing type-checked `<select [formField]>` usages (including string literal unions, string enums, and generic string-constrained fields) continue to compile and behave identically at runtime.

## Other information

- Related to #68217.
- Also related to existing draft PR #68442 (which allowed `string | number | null` covariantly, creating ambiguity for `string | null` models).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(forms): support binding numeric values to `<select>` in signal forms" (#72143)

Issues.Title: fix(core): do not drop nested @defer child blocks while parent hydrates
Issues.Body:
In `getParentBlockHydrationQueue`, PR #58722 breaks out of the ancestor loop before calling `hydrationQueue.unshift(currentBlockId)` when it encounters an ancestor `@defer` block that is already hydrating. Because of that, `hydrationQueue` never contains the hydrating ancestor, only the unhydrated descendants below it.

`triggerHydrationFromBlockName` still contains a `hydrationQueue.shift()` added in PR #60203 under the assumption that the hydrating parent sat at index 0. When `parentBlockPromise` is non-null, that shifts off the first unhydrated child block instead: in a 2-level nested `@defer` block it empties the queue and drops the replay event, and in a 3-level hierarchy (immediate inside interaction inside immediate) it drops the middle block so both inner blocks stay dehydrated.

Remove the stale `hydrationQueue.shift()` call and add regression specs in `incremental_hydration_spec.ts`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(core): do not drop nested @defer child blocks while parent hydrates" (#72123)

Issues.Title: [Feature request]: Resource based suspense with @await blocks in @boundary
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? core, compiler, compiler-cli, router, common, platform-server ### Description **Builds on:** - `@boundary` / `@error` (developer preview, 22.2) - `resource()` - Router resources (developer preview, 22.2) - Router error boundaries (developer preview, 22.3) **Scope:** compiler, template syntax, runtime (render3), resource and input types, router integration, DevTools > Implementation notes and prior art (React Suspense, Solid 2.0, the router precedents) are in the first comment, to keep this body within GitHub's size limit. #### 1. Summary This proposal adds **coordinated loading states** to Angular templates. It extends the existing `@boundary` error boundary, so the same block that catches errors also manages pending data. It has three parts: 1. **The `@await` block.** A template block that unwraps one or more resources into plain values. Inside the block, the values have their loaded type, not `T | undefined`. The block registers its resources with the nearest boundary. Its content renders, and later updates, only when the resources are ready. 2. **A `@pending` block on `@boundary`.** The `@pending` block is the fallback. A boundary that has a `@pending` block coordinates every `@await` registered below it. It reveals them together, keeps stale content on screen while they refresh, and resets when the content's identity changes (`track`). It also exposes a `$pending` context variable. 3. **Configuration.** `provideBoundaries()` sets app-wide defaults for timing in core. In the router, `withBoundaries()` combines today's error options with pending coordination at each ``. ```html @boundary (track userId(); let refreshing = $pending) { @if (refreshing) { } @await (user = userResource; posts = feedResource) {

{{ user.name }}

} } @pending (after 150ms; minimum 400ms) { } @error (let e; reset = $reset) { } ``` Suspension is **explicit**. A resource only takes part when it is read through `@await`. Reading `resource.value()` directly behaves as it does today. Angular's signal graph does not change: pending and error stay properties of the resource object, not hidden state in the graph. #### 2. Motivation ##### 2.1 The problem today Resources made async data first-class in Angular. Each resource exposes `value()`, `status()`, `error()`, `isLoading()`, `hasValue()` and `snapshot()`. Every template that reads a resource handles those states itself, which leads to the following problems. - **Loading-state sprawl.** Each component writes its own `@if (res.isLoading())` and `@if (res.error())` branches. A page with five resources shows five spinners that appear and disappear independently. - **Inconsistent states on screen (tearing).** When a resource reloads, parts of the UI that depend on it update at different times. A header can show the new user while a sibling list still shows the previous user's data. - **Flashing.** Reloads that resolve quickly make spinners flash. A new request clears a resource's value, so content that depends on it disappears and the layout jumps. - **No coordination across components.** Resources are often created or injected several components deep. Showing one fallback for a section means passing loading signals up through inputs and outputs. For resources injected through DI, that wiring doesn't exist at all. - **`T | undefined` everywhere.** Without a `defaultValue`, `value()` is `T | undefined`. Templates fill up with `?.` and `@if (res.hasValue())` guards, even in areas that only make sense once the data is ready. A `defaultValue` removes `undefined` from the type, but templates then show the default (for example an empty list) as if it were data while loading. - **Errors are handled separately from loading.** `@boundary` already catches resource errors, because `value()` throws in the error state. It knows nothing about pending state, so loading and error handling are written in two different ways. - **Non-blocking route data flashes.** When a `nonBlocking()` route resource's params change on navigation, the new request clears its value, and the page flashes ([#70809](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/70809)). - The maintainers' answers were to use a blocking resource, or to keep the previous value with a snapshot in userland. They noted that the router has no opinion on how the transition should look, and that keeping old values would be "very incorrect for many situations", for example "showing data for /user/1 after navigation to /user/2 is complete". Suspense and transitions were mentioned in passing; the suggested mitigation was a `waitFor` option ([PR #70539](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/70539)). - The choice between keeping old content and showing a placeholder belongs to a specific area of UI, which neither the router nor the resource knows about. Whatever that area chooses, it must never show data for a different route (§5.6). ##### 2.2 What Angular already coordinates, and where it stops Angular already provides coordination, freezing and fallback UI, but only at the router level: - **Route-level coordination.** Router resources (`withRouterResources()`, `Route.resources`) load in parallel across the matched route hierarchy. By default they are *blocking*: the router waits for them before activating the route, and the component receives a plain `T`. - **Freezing during navigation.** While a navigation is pending, resources on `ActivatedRoute` show the state they had when the navigation started. The previous screen stays stable until the navigation commits or is rolled back. - **Error fallbacks at the outlet.** Router error boundaries (`withErrorBoundaries()`, `Route.errorComponent`) replace a failed routed component with a fallback component. None of these reach below the outlet. Once a route is active, component-owned resources, non-blocking route resources and refreshes that happen without a navigation have no coordination, no freezing and no shared fallback. This proposal brings the same guarantees to any part of a template: | Router level (exists) | Template level (proposed) | |---|---| | Router coordinates route data across the route hierarchy | `@boundary` coordinates resources across nested components | | Blocking resources delay route activation | `@await` delays rendering of data-dependent content | | `nonBlocking()` hands loading state to the component | `@pending` gives a coordinated fallback for that state | | Route resources frozen during navigation | Revealed content kept on screen during any refresh | | `errorComponent` handles failures of the routed component | `@error` handles failures local to a boundary | The two levels complement each other. The router stays responsible for navigation-time data, and boundaries take over once the route is active (§5.6). ##### 2.3 Why this needs the framework Userland can't build this correctly, for these reasons. - **Block syntax can't be extended.** `@boundary` is compiler syntax and accepts no parameters today. Userland can't add `@pending` or new parameters to it. - **Freezing needs view ownership.** Freezing content means skipping the update pass of views you don't own. With ``, the content's views belong to the parent, so a wrapper component can't freeze them. - **No commit phase.** Angular's template instructions write to the DOM as they run. Avoiding half-updated views needs a compiler guarantee that every operand of a block is evaluated before any binding in that block. - **Correct types need the compiler.** The type checker has to know that the block's content only runs when the value has loaded. - **Parallel loading needs runtime control.** A component's `resource()` starts its request from an effect tied to the view that declares the component. Starting nested components' requests before the parent's data has resolved ("create early, bind late", §5.5) means running those effects while skipping the view's bindings. Only change detection can do that. #### 3. Goals and non-goals ##### Goals - **Explicit opt-in.** Suspension happens only where `@await` is written. - **Coordination across components.** Resources read anywhere below a boundary, at any depth and however they were obtained (input, DI, local field), take part in the same pending state. - **One place for policy.** Fallback, timing, stale-content limits and identity resets live on `@boundary` and `@pending`. - **All-or-nothing updates.** No `@await` block is ever half-updated, and blocks under the same boundary are revealed and released together. - **Parallel data loading.** Nesting components inside `@await` must not turn independent requests into a waterfall. - **Typed values.** Values unwrapped by `@await` have the resource's loaded type. - **Easy to inspect.** DevTools and diagnostics show which resources hold which boundary, and why. ##### Non-goals - Implicit pending propagation through the signal graph (§10.1). - Changing how the router handles navigation-time data. Blocking route resources, navigation freezing and `NavigationError` keep their current behaviour. - Suspending on raw Promises or Observables. Resources are the supported protocol, and `rxResource`, `httpResource` and similar adapters cover other sources. - Suspending code in the component class (computeds, effects, methods). Class code keeps reading resources as it does today. - A programmatic API for boundaries (§11). - Replacing `@defer`. `@defer` controls *when code loads and when views are created*. Suspense controls *when data-dependent content is revealed or updated*. ### Proposed solution #### 4. Design overview | Concern | Construct | Placed | |---|---|---| | Unwrapping data, all-or-nothing updates | `@await (x = res; …) { }` | Deep, where data is read | | Fallback, timing, stale-content limit, identity, grouping | `@boundary (…) { } @pending (…) { } @error { }` | High, at layout or section level | | App-wide defaults | `provideBoundaries()`, router `withBoundaries()` | Application config | The split is deliberate. `@await` blocks are **local**: each one unwraps values and freezes its own small area. A `@boundary` with `@pending` **coordinates**: it groups every `@await` registered beneath it, decides what users see while they are pending, and releases them together. Two pieces of data are "part of the same suspense" when they are registered with the same boundary, not when they appear in the same block. Component authors and library authors follow one rule: **put `@await` where you read the data.** The block joins whatever boundary the consumer placed around the component. Nothing else is needed. #### 5. Detailed design ##### 5.1 The `@await` block ###### Syntax ```html @await (alias = expression; alias2 = expression2) { …content using alias and alias2… } ``` - One or more `alias = expression` pairs, separated by semicolons. - Aliases are scoped to the block's content, like `@if (…; as x)`. - **Operands are independent.** An operand can't refer to another alias in the same header, and the compiler reports an error if it does, so no operand waits on another alias. Data that depends on another alias goes in a nested block, which makes the dependency visible in the template: ```html @await (user = userResource) { @await (posts = user.feedResource) { … } } ``` - `@await` has no `@pending` or `@error` blocks of its own. Fallbacks and errors belong to the boundary. ###### Accepted operands An operand must be **resource-shaped**, which is checked structurally: ```ts interface ResourceLike { readonly snapshot: Signal>; readonly [ɵRESOURCE_LOADED]?: readonly [L]; // type-only marker, see "Typing" reload?(): boolean; } ``` - **`snapshot`** reads the status and the value together and never throws. `Resource` already exposes it, so `resource`, `rxResource`, `httpResource`, `resourceFromSnapshots`, router resources and userland wrappers all qualify without a framework brand. - **`reload()` is optional**, because the read-only types (`Resource`, and the type `asReadonly()` returns) don't declare it, and userland wrappers may not have one. It is only used by `$reset` (§5.2.7). - **Compile time.** The generated type-check code passes each operand through an intrinsic, `ɵawait()`. Anything that isn't resource-shaped is a template type error. - **Runtime (dev mode).** A shape check produces a clear error for operands that get past type checking, for example through `any`. - **Plain signals, Promises and Observables are rejected.** None of them has a `snapshot`. - A `Signal` is never pending, so awaiting one would quietly do nothing. - A Promise has no synchronous status, and its identity is not stable across checks. ###### Typing Inside the content, each alias has the resource's **loaded type**: the type its loader produces, without the `undefined` that the resource adds while nothing has loaded. Today that distinction is lost. A resource without `defaultValue` is typed `ResourceRef`, which is the same for a loader returning `Promise` and one returning `Promise`. This proposal keeps it with a second, defaulted type parameter on the resource types: ```ts interface Resource { readonly [ɵRESOURCE_LOADED]?: readonly [L]; // value, status, error, isLoading, snapshot and hasValue are unchanged } // overload without defaultValue function resource(options: ResourceOptions): ResourceRef; ``` ```ts userResource = resource({loader: () => fetchUser()}); // ResourceRef maybeUser = resource({loader: () => findUser()}); // ResourceRef hits = resource({loader: () => search(), defaultValue: []}); // ResourceRef ``` ```html @await (u = userResource) { … } @await (m = maybeUser) { … } @await (h = hits) { … } ``` - **When the marker is missing**, the alias has the resource's `T`, which is always sound. This covers userland wrappers without the marker, and user annotations such as `input>()`. A child component's input keeps the loaded type when it is declared as `Resource`. - **Known gap:** calling `set(undefined)` on a writable resource whose loaded type excludes `undefined` produces a `local` resource holding `undefined`. The block still renders it, and dev mode warns (§5.8). ###### When a block is ready Readiness depends only on the resource's **status**, never on `hasValue()`. A `defaultValue` makes `hasValue()` true while loading, but it is not loaded data. | Status | Before the block's first reveal | After the block has been revealed | |---|---|---| | `resolved`, `local` | **Ready** | **Ready**: the content updates | | `loading`, `reloading` | **Waiting** | **Refreshing**: the boundary's stale policy applies (§5.2.4) | | `idle` | **Hidden**: doesn't hold the boundary | **Hidden**: content kept alive off-screen; doesn't hold the boundary | | `error` | **Error** (§5.2.7) | **Error** (§5.2.7) | - **`reloading` waits before the first reveal.** A resource can be `reloading` after an error, when it has no value. A block created while a shared resource reloads waits for the fresh value instead of showing an old one. - **`idle` means "no data requested",** for example a search with an empty query, so the block shows nothing and doesn't hold its boundary. "Not available yet" is expressed by `params` throwing `ResourceParamsStatus.LOADING` (§5.5), which makes the resource `loading`. Authors who want an empty state write it outside the block: ```html @if (results.status() === 'idle') {

Type to search

} @await (r = results) { } ``` - **A hidden block that starts loading** follows its boundary's phase (§5.2.2). It holds the reveal while the boundary is pending, and it is a late block, hidden until ready, while the boundary shows content. ###### Semantics 1. **Unit of freezing.** Each control-flow block has its own embedded view, and the `@await` content view is the unit that renders or freezes. While the block is waiting or refreshing, its content's bindings are not updated, apart from early inputs (§5.5). Content outside the block, including siblings in the same template, is unaffected. 2. **All-or-nothing.** All operands are read before any binding in the content, so the content is never half-updated against a mix of old and new values. 3. **Registration.** When it is created, the block registers its operands with the nearest coordinating boundary (§5.2.8). It re-registers when an operand's identity changes, and unregisters when it is destroyed. 4. **Typing guarantee.** The content's bindings only run in the *ready* state, so an alias always holds loaded data. 5. **Per-row suspension.** Inside `@for`, each row's `@await` registers separately (§5.2.2): ```html @for (item of items(); track item.id) { @await (details = item.detailsResource) { } } ``` ###### What `@await` does *not* do - It doesn't affect class code. A `computed` that reads `userResource.value()` still sees `undefined` (or the `defaultValue`) while loading, and rethrows in the error state. - It doesn't catch errors from non-resource sources. Existing `@boundary` error handling covers those. - It doesn't start or cancel requests. Resource lifecycles are unchanged. ##### 5.2 Pending states on `@boundary` ###### 5.2.1 Full syntax ```html @boundary (track ; let = $pending) { …content… } @pending (after ; minimum ; stale none | | unlimited) { …fallback… } @error (let e; reset = $reset; when ) { … } @error { … } ``` - Every parameter is optional, and parameters can appear in any order. - **A boundary coordinates pending state only if it has a `@pending` block.** A `@boundary` without one behaves exactly as it does today, and passes `@await` registrations up to the next coordinating boundary. - **A boundary without `@error` blocks doesn't catch errors.** Errors pass through it to the next boundary out, so a pending-only section boundary never destroys its content because of an error. This changes today's behaviour (§5.9). - **To coordinate without a fallback,** use an empty `@pending { }`. Blocks are still revealed together and stale content is still kept, but nothing is shown while the boundary is pending. ###### 5.2.2 Boundary and block states Each `@await` block and each coordinating boundary has a small set of phases. | Block phase | Meaning | |---|---| | `waiting` | Not ready and never shown. Bindings aren't applied. | | `ready` | Showing current data. | | `frozen` | Showing its last data while its resources refresh. | | `hidden` | Content kept alive but not shown: the resource is `idle`, or the block is a *late block* that isn't ready yet. | | Boundary phase | Meaning | |---|---| | `pending` | No registered block is showing content, and at least one is waiting. The fallback rules of §5.2.3 apply. | | `revealed` | The content is shown, and every showing block is ready. | | `refreshing` | The content is shown, and at least one showing block is frozen. `$pending` is `true`. | | `stale-fallback` | A refresh outlasted `stale`. The content is kept alive off the DOM, and the fallback is shown. | | `error` | An `@error` block is shown. | **"First load" is the `pending` phase**: the boundary has no block showing content. A boundary whose blocks were all hidden (for example because their resources are `idle`) is pending again when one of them starts loading. Whether "first load" should instead happen once per boundary, or be tracked per block, is open question 1 (§11). | Event | When the boundary is… | Result | |---|---|---| | A block registers, or a hidden block starts loading | `pending` | It holds the reveal. | | | `revealed` or `refreshing` | It is a **late block**: hidden until ready, sets `$pending`, doesn't hold other blocks' release, doesn't start the `stale` timer. | | A showing block's resource starts loading or reloading | `revealed` | The block freezes. The boundary moves to `refreshing`, and the `stale` timer starts. | | Every frozen block is ready | `refreshing` | All frozen blocks update **in one pass**, and the boundary moves to `revealed`. Blocks discovered during that pass are late blocks. | | `stale` elapses | `refreshing` | `stale-fallback`. | | Every non-hidden block is ready | `pending` or `stale-fallback` | The content is attached (after `minimum`), and the boundary moves to `revealed`. | | A showing block's resource becomes `idle` | any shown phase | The block is hidden and stops counting. | | The `track` value changes | any | The content is recreated, and the boundary moves to `pending`. | | A resource errors | any | The error is raised from the block's view (§5.2.7). | - **`@for` rows.** Each row's block registers separately and follows the same rules. Rows are revealed together on first load, and rows added later are late blocks. - **Hidden content** is frozen (§5.5) and kept until the block is destroyed. ###### 5.2.3 First load: `after` and `minimum` While the boundary is `pending`, it shows `@pending` instead of its content. The content is still **created** in the background (§5.5), so requests start and nested blocks are discovered. It is attached to the DOM only when every block that isn't hidden is ready, so nothing half-loaded is ever visible. - **`after `:** wait this long before showing the fallback. If everything is ready sooner, the content appears directly, with no flash. - **`minimum `:** once shown, keep the fallback on screen for at least this long, to avoid a flicker. These have the same meaning as the options on `@defer`'s `@loading` block. How the timers interact: - **An error during `minimum`** waits until `minimum` ends, as in `@defer`, so the fallback never flickers straight into an error. - **A `track` change during `after`:** the old content is already destroyed, so nothing is shown until `after` elapses, then the fallback. - **Reveal batching** (§5.4) is measured from the last reveal. The first reveal is never delayed. ###### 5.2.4 Refreshes: `stale` A **refresh** happens when a block that is showing content needs new data, for example because a registered resource's params changed or `reload()` was called. By default, the boundary **keeps the content on screen**: - Refreshing `@await` blocks are frozen and keep showing their last values. - The rest of the boundary's content keeps updating, which is what makes a "refreshing" indicator possible (§5.2.5). - `$pending` is `true`. - When every frozen block is ready again, they all update **together, in one pass**. `stale` limits how long stale content may stay on screen: ```html } @pending (after 150ms; minimum 400ms) { … } } @pending (after 150ms; minimum 400ms; stale 1s) { … } } @pending (after 150ms; minimum 400ms; stale none) { … } } @pending (stale unlimited) { … } ``` - **When the fallback replaces stale content,** the content views stay alive but are detached from the DOM. **Component state survives; DOM state may not**: focus, selection, scroll positions, `
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Feature request]: Resource based suspense with @await blocks in @boundary" (#72140)

Issues.Title: fix(core): safely handle server platform destruction on aborted SSR requests
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

When an SSR server immediately destroys `PlatformRef` on request abort (e.g. via `@angular/ssr`), several framework paths can crash the Node.js process with `uncaughtException` or `unhandledRejection`, or leave in-flight requests open:

- `bootstrap()` looks up `ENABLE_ROOT_COMPONENT_BOOTSTRAP` after `ApplicationInitStatus.donePromise` without checking `envInjector.destroyed`, throwing `NG0205`.
- `ApplicationInitStatus` does not unsubscribe observable initializers or settle `donePromise` when destroyed.
- `INTERNAL_APPLICATION_ERROR_HANDLER` throws via `setTimeout(() => { throw e; })` when `injector.destroyed` and no prior error has cached `userErrorHandler`, terminating Node.js SSR servers.
- `PendingTasks.run()` reports post-destroy promise rejections to `ErrorHandler`.
- `FetchBackend` does not abort in-flight `fetch` requests on `DestroyRef.onDestroy`, and emitting `complete()` on stream cancellation triggers `EmptyError` in `firstValueFrom`/`lastValueFrom`.
- `Router.dispose()` does not unsubscribe active `setupNavigations` transitions, leaving guards and resolvers running after platform teardown.
- `renderInternal()` reports rejections from async `BEFORE_APP_SERIALIZED` hooks and calls `renderToString()` even if the platform was destroyed mid-hook.

Related issue: angular/angular-cli#34754

## What is the new behavior?

- **`@angular/core`**:
  - `ApplicationInitStatus` unsubscribes observable initializers on `DestroyRef.onDestroy`, settles `donePromise` without setting `done = true`, stops remaining initializers if destroyed, and ignores late post-destroy rejections.
  - `bootstrap()`, `internalCreateApplication()`, and `PlatformRef.bootstrapModule()` settle cleanly with the destroyed `ApplicationRef` / `NgModuleRef` without bootstrapping root components when destroyed before or during initialization.
  - `PendingTasks.run()` checks `DestroyRef.destroyed` before reporting errors.
  - `INTERNAL_APPLICATION_ERROR_HANDLER` logs via `console.error('ERROR', e)` on the server when destroyed without a cached `ErrorHandler` instead of throwing from `setTimeout`.
- **`@angular/common/http`**:
  - `FetchBackend` unsubscribes on `DestroyRef.onDestroy` to abort in-flight `fetch` calls and clear timeouts without emitting `complete()` or `error()`, cancels body streams on destroy, and skips initiating requests when already destroyed.
- **`@angular/router`**:
  - `Router.dispose()` unsubscribes active `setupNavigations` transitions (after detaching the navigation event listener) and `withEnabledBlockingInitialNavigation()` skips starting navigation if the injector was destroyed while awaiting `LOCATION_INITIALIZED`.
- **`@angular/platform-server`**:
  - `renderInternal()`, `renderApplication()`, and `renderModule()` return `''` early when destroyed before or during async `BEFORE_APP_SERIALIZED` hooks, suppress post-destroy `ErrorHandler` reporting, and ensure `asyncDestroyPlatform()` always resolves safely.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

## Other information

Companion `@angular/ssr` PR: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/34768

Issues.Title: fix(core): respect styling precedence for namespaced CSS custom properties
Issues.Body:
Hi Angular team 👋 This fixes a case where clearing a CSS custom property binding also removes the static value it was overriding. For example, with `provideCssVarNamespacing('ns')`, both declarations below target `--ns_x`: ```html
``` When `color()` changes from `'blue'` to `undefined`, the property should return to `green`. Currently, Angular removes it because the styling code compares the compiled binding name (`--%NS%x`) with the literal name (`--ns_x`) and misses the match. This change records potential matches when Angular registers the bindings, then uses the application's namespace to resolve them during updates. Bindings for unrelated custom properties can still skip the priority lookup. The regression tests cover static styles, style maps, and host bindings, both with and without a namespace. They also cover two applications sharing the same component and a custom renderer that delegates DOM writes while keeping its own `data` object. I verified the fix in Chromium and Firefox. The core Render3 and acceptance tests also pass. Fixes #71806

Issues.Title: fix(core): clear reactive consumer when creating node injectables
Issues.Body: Please note that this fixes a **real** production issue; it wasn't found speculatively through AI code analysis. `R3Injector.hydrate` clears the active reactive consumer before it runs a provider factory. `getNodeInjectable` does not. It already saves and restores four other things, but not the consumer. So creating an injectable is not reactive with the environment injector, but it is reactive with the node injector. This only shows up when a node-level provider or view provider is created late, after the view already exists. That happens through `injector.get()`, through `runInInjectionContext()`, and when a signal query reads a provider with `read:`. Components and directives are created in `renderView`, where the consumer is already null, and `ɵɵpipe` calls the pipe factory itself, so those do not go through this path. Here is a component with a node-level provider that is created late: ```ts @Component({ template: '{{ label }}', providers: [Lazy], }) class App { private injector = inject(Injector); get label() { return this.injector.get(Lazy).label(); } } ``` Two problems come from this. First, a signal write in a constructor throws NG0600. The template consumer does not allow writes. A `computed` does not allow them either, which is how a signal query hits this too. Second, a signal read in a constructor becomes a dependency of the consumer around it. Another signal can then make that consumer dirty, and it keeps the consumer alive. There is no error, so nobody sees it. We saw the first problem in production. `Lazy` is our code with new names. A field initializer turned an observable into a signal: ```ts class Lazy { // field initializer, runs inside `getNodeInjectable` readonly label = toSignal(this.data.label$, { initialValue: '' }); } ``` `toSignal` subscribes right away, inside its own call. It does not wait for an effect. Our source emitted a value during that `subscribe`. So the `next` handler of `toSignal` called `.set` before the constructor finished, and the template consumer of `App` was still active. Two things made this hard to find. The source did not look synchronous. It ends with a `forkJoin`, and `forkJoin` emits from its finalize handler. So the value came during teardown and not from a simple `of()`. Also, `publishSignalConfiguration` builds the message only when `ngDevMode` is on. In production it throws `RuntimeError(-600, '')`. Our report had only `NG0600` and a short minified stack. The last frames were the `toSignal` callback and RxJS code. The stack did not show our class or our component. Now `getNodeInjectable` clears the consumer around the factory call and restores it in the `finally` block that is already there. This is what the environment injector does.

Issues.Title: fix(core): avoid NG0502 for nodes after `<ng-content>` or `@let` in content that is not projected
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements: - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) No docs change: the fix makes a supported case (content that is not projected) work as documented. ## PR Type What kind of change does this PR introduce? - [x] Bugfix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? Issue Number: #72129 With hydration enabled, server rendering fails with `NG0502: During serialization, Angular was unable to find an element in the DOM` when a node follows an `` slot or a `@let` declaration inside content that is not projected. For example, a component places `` and then an `@if` block inside ``, and `app-container` renders its own `` inside an `@if` that is false. An `` slot or a `@let` declaration has no DOM node, so `serializeLView` stores a full path for the node that follows it ([`annotate.ts`, projection branch](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/73916540c1688c0463617ef1469bf63adb0a628f/packages/core/src/hydration/annotate.ts#L707-L722)). It did so even when that node is disconnected from the DOM, and `calcPathForNode` throws for a node it can't find. ## What is the new behavior? One rule decides which disconnected nodes are skipped. `serializeLView` already annotates content-projected nodes that are disconnected from the DOM as disconnected ([line 613](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/73916540c1688c0463617ef1469bf63adb0a628f/packages/core/src/hydration/annotate.ts#L613)), and the client creates those nodes instead of hydrating them. - **The rule:** that check moves into a helper, `isDisconnectedContentProjectedNode(tNode, lView)`, used both for that annotation and for the nodes after an `` slot or a `@let` declaration. - **What is skipped:** after a slot or a declaration, the loop that already skips other slots and declarations also skips the nodes annotated as disconnected. The first connected node after them gets the path, so the client can locate it even when its previous sibling is disconnected. - **What is kept:** any other node missing from the DOM keeps the NG0502 serialization error, for example a node in the component's own template that a third-party script removed. - **Unchanged:** the projection-head check, which handles a different case. ```diff - if (isDisconnectedNode(tNode, lView) && isContentProjectedNode(tNode)) { + if (isDisconnectedContentProjectedNode(tNode, lView)) { appendDisconnectedNodeIndex(ngh, tNode); continue; } ... while ( nextTNode !== null && - nextTNode.type & (TNodeType.Projection | TNodeType.LetDeclaration) + (nextTNode.type & (TNodeType.Projection | TNodeType.LetDeclaration) || + isDisconnectedContentProjectedNode(nextTNode, lView)) ) { nextTNode = nextTNode.next; } ... +function isDisconnectedContentProjectedNode(tNode: TNode, lView: LView): boolean { + return isDisconnectedNode(tNode, lView) && isContentProjectedNode(tNode); +} ``` Tests in `packages/platform-server/test/full_app_hydration_spec.ts`, under `partial projection`, next to "should support cases when some element nodes are not projected (@if)": - **"should support nodes after `` when the content is not projected (@if)":** - **Components:** a container (`@if (open) { }`), a wrapper (`@if (true) {

after

}`), and an app that projects text into the wrapper. - **Assertions:** SSR succeeds, the projected content is absent from the server HTML, all nodes are claimed for hydration and the client and server contents match. Once `open` becomes `true`, the projected text and `

after

` render inside the container. - **"should support nodes after @let when the content is not projected":** - **Components:** the same container, with `@let label = 'after';` followed by `@if (true) {

{{ label }}

}` as its content. The `@let` is read in a nested view, so the compiler keeps it as a `@let` node. - **Assertions:** the same checks, then `

after

` renders once the container opens. - **`describe('disconnected nodes that are not content projected')`:** pins the kept diagnostic. A directive removes an element from the DOM on the server, as a third-party script would. The element sits in the projector component's own template, so it is not content projected. - **"should throw NG0502 for a node after `` that was removed from the DOM":** the projector template is `

after

`. - **"should throw NG0502 for a node after @let that was removed from the DOM":** the projector template is `@let label = 'after';` followed by `

` with the `@let` read in a nested `@if`. - **How they assert:** both expect `ssr(...)` to reject with `NG0502: During serialization, Angular was unable to find an element in the DOM`. The promise is resolved to its error before the assertion, as `getHydrationError` does in this file, so a render that succeeds fails the test. - **`describe('connected nodes after disconnected nodes')`:** a connected node that follows an `` slot or a `@let` declaration and one or more disconnected content-projected nodes. Each test checks that the connected node is claimed for hydration (`verifyAllNodesClaimedForHydration`), that the client and server contents match, and that its text renders. - **Multi-slot:** ``, a `

` in a hidden slot, then a `

` in a visible slot; and the same after a `@let`. These already hydrated before the review change, because `

` is a slot head and gets a path from the projection head handling. - **Same slot:** ``, a `

` in a hidden slot, then a `

` projected into the same slot as the ``. The `

`'s predecessor in the slot is the projection node, which both the projection head handling and `conditionallyAnnotateNodePath` skip, so only this loop can anchor it. - **Removed node:** `

ok
` in projected content, and the same with a `@let`. `//packages/platform-server/test:test` results, 427 specs: | `annotate.ts` | Result | Failing tests | | --- | --- | --- | | `main`, without the fix | 7 failures | the two original tests and the five `connected nodes after disconnected nodes` tests, with NG0502 from `serializeLView` → `appendSerializedNodePath` → `calcPathForNode` | | Skipping every disconnected node after the loop (`!isDisconnectedNode(nextTNode, lView)`) | 2 failures (422 specs, before the new tests) | the two diagnostic tests: the server render succeeds, so the NG0502 is lost | | Skipping the next node only, without advancing the loop (first commit of this PR) | 3 failures | the same-slot case and the two removed-node cases, with NG0500 on the client | | This PR | 0 failures | none | All targets under `//packages/platform-server/...` pass with this PR, as do `//packages/core/test:test`, `//packages/core/test/acceptance:acceptance` and `//packages/core/test/bundling/hydration:test` / `:symbol_test`. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [ ] Yes - [x] No ## Other information - **Formatting:** `ng-dev format` also reflows one existing template in `full_app_hydration_spec.ts` (`{{ spanText }}.` becomes `{{ spanText }}.`). That file is not Prettier-clean on `main` with the pinned Prettier 3.10.1, and the pre-commit formatter applies the change. It only removes whitespace inside a closing tag, so the template renders the same. - **Test inputs:** the test components use `@Input()` instead of signal inputs. This target compiles the specs with TypeScript and the components JIT, so `input()` fields are not recognised there (NG0303), and no other test in the file uses them. Component state uses `signal`, and updates use `await appRef.whenStable()`. - **Out of scope:** a separate problem with content that is not projected. With `
` in such content, server rendering succeeds even without this fix, but once the content is shown after hydration the `
` stays empty. `ɵɵprojection` does not apply the projection while hydrating, even though that `
` was disconnected on the server and is created fresh on the client. This PR does not change that behavior. It is reported in #72132.

Issues.Title: fix(core): drain queued replay events during defer hydration
Issues.Body:
When combining `withIncrementalHydration()` and `withEventReplay()`, events on `@defer` blocks can be dropped in three race windows:

- A live event arriving while a block is already hydrating via a non-replay trigger returns early from `triggerHydrationFromBlockName` and never drains `EVENT_REPLAY_QUEUE`.
- An early click before bootstrap is lost when `@defer (hydrate on immediate)` finishes hydrating and strips listeners synchronously before `whenStable().then(initEventReplay)` runs on a later microtask.
- An early click replayed while `triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` is parked at `await appRef.whenStable()` for another pending task is either skipped or replayed out of order if listener cleanup is not deferred before parking.

Remove the unused `replayQueuedEventsFn` parameter from `triggerHydrationFromBlockName` and `triggerHydrationForBlockQueue`, drain and compact `EVENT_REPLAY_QUEUE` before and after `await appRef.whenStable()` inside a `try/finally` cleanup guard (dropping disconnected or `ngb`-stripped items), guard `appRef.destroyed` after `initEventReplay`, and add an `INITIAL_EVENT_REPLAY_STATE` token so `DehydratedBlockRegistry` defers listener cleanup before parking until initial replay finishes (or `appRef.onDestroy()`, matching `EAGER_CONTENT_LISTENERS_KEY`) without eagerly resolving `DEHYDRATED_BLOCK_REGISTRY` or prematurely tearing down the event contract. Add deterministic regression specs in `event_replay_spec.ts`.

Fixes #71296
Fixes #72006

Issues.Title: fix(core): clear hydration state per instance when projecting into skip-hydration blocks
Issues.Body:
When projecting content indirectly into a component with `ngSkipHydration`, `applyProjectionRecursive` previously mutated `nodeToProject.flags` with `TNodeFlags.inSkipHydrationBlock` on the host component's shared `TView`. That crashed with a `TypeError` on empty `<ng-content>` slots (`nodeToProject` is `null`), only annotated the head projected node (dropping subsequent `projectionNext` siblings, `<ng-container>` children, and multi-root `@if`/`@for` views after `clearElementContents` detached them), and polluted subsequent instances of the host component. Meanwhile, `isInSkipHydrationBlock` had a typo checking `tNode` instead of `currentTNode` in its ancestor walk; fixing that typo while shared `TView` mutation remained regressed wrapper `<div>` templates into duplicate DOM and `i18n` crashes.

Fix the `currentTNode` typo in `isInSkipHydrationBlock`, stop mutating the shared `TView` in `applyProjectionRecursive` (guarding `nodeToProject === null`), and clear per-instance hydration state when projecting in creation mode using a registered `clearProjectedNodeHydrationState` hook in `hydration/views.ts` (wired by `enableHydrationRuntimeSupport` so `node_manipulation.ts` keeps no hydration imports and non-hydration apps make no DOM calls). Clearing `DEHYDRATED_VIEWS`, resetting `SSR_BLOCK_STATE` on projected `@defer` containers, and recording projected `ViewContainerRef` hosts in `disconnectedNodes` lets projected `@if`, `@for`, `i18n`/ICU, `ViewContainerRef`, and `@defer` blocks fall back cleanly to creation mode while non-skipped instances still reuse SSR DOM. Incremental `@defer (hydrate on ...)` blocks projected indirectly into `ngSkipHydration` remain a known out-of-scope limitation. Add regression specs in `full_app_hydration_spec.ts` and update bundle symbol goldens.

Issues.Title: fix(core): skip animate.enter on hydrated DOM nodes
Issues.Body:
During SSR hydration, `ɵɵanimateEnter` and `ɵɵanimateEnterListener` only check `ngServerMode`, `areAnimationSupported`, and `areAnimationsDisabled`. Elements and component hosts reused from server-rendered HTML therefore replay their enter animations on client bootstrap (and incremental `@defer` hydration), causing a visible flash after the SSR HTML has already painted.

Populate the root component view's `HYDRATION` slot in `component_ref.ts` before invoking host bindings (splitting `createDirectivesInstances` into `instantiateAllDirectives` and `invokeDirectivesHostBindings`), and add an `isHydratingNode(lView, tNode)` guard in `animation.ts` using only existing `render3` state so CSR bundles pull in no hydration code or `ngh` DOM queries. Skip queueing enter animations on hydrated template nodes, hydrated root and child component hosts, and reused `ngSkipHydration` host elements, while still running them on dynamically created views/components, recreated children inside `ngSkipHydration`, and nodes in `DISCONNECTED_NODES`. Add browser acceptance specs in `animation_spec.ts`.

Fixes #72146

cc @thePunderWoman

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): expose AnalyzerHost protocol and auto-select WASM in preprocessor
Issues.Body:
Bundler integrations need a public TypeScript host interface and pump-loop driver to supply
asynchronous module resolutions and source text to the WASM analyzer without reading the local
filesystem or requiring a tsconfig.

Define AnalyzerHost, ResolveRequest, ResolveResult, LoadRequest, LoadResult, ResourceRequest,
ResourceResolveResult, HostItemError, ModuleFormat, and ModuleRef across analyzer_wasm.ts, types.ts,
and api.ts. Teach WasmAnalyzer.pumpLoop to dispatch hostRequests batches concurrently via
Promise.all, map rejected batch promises and mismatched result counts into per-slot error objects,
avoid spinning while stalled on in-flight host batches, and resume pumping via provideHostResults.

Add LoadAnalyzerOptions.host to createAnalyzer so providing a custom host validates mutually
exclusive filesystem/tsconfig options, auto-selects the WASM backend when backend is omitted, and
constructs WasmAnalyzer in BatchingHost mode. Widen IAnalyzer and HybridCompiler direct-entry and
invalidation methods to accept ModuleRef and idKind.

Issues.Title: feat(compiler-cli): type-check custom elements declared in HTMLElementTagNameMap
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Using a Web Component / custom element in an Angular template currently requires adding `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` to the component/NgModule, which suppresses element/property schema errors (`NG8001`/`NG8002`) but leaves property bindings completely untyped — even when the custom element already registers its tag name and interface in TypeScript's global `HTMLElementTagNameMap`.

## What is the new behavior?

Automatically recognize and type-check custom elements (non-Angular elements with a dash in their tag name) that are declared in TypeScript's global `HTMLElementTagNameMap`, without requiring a compiler flag or `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA`, in both **`ngtsc`** and **`ngp`** (the Rust/TS preprocessor):

- **Discovery**:
  - In `ngtsc`: `TemplateTypeCheckerImpl` resolves TypeScript's global `HTMLElementTagNameMap` once per program and collects lowercase tag names containing `-` (excluding built-in Angular elements `ng-container`, `ng-content`, `ng-template` and non-HTML namespaces like `:svg:` / `:math:`).
  - In `ngp`: `ng-analyze` exposes a cached `QueryKey::KnownCustomElements` query across WASM, N-API, and Sidecar transports that extracts global `HTMLElementTagNameMap` entries from program `.ts` files, tsconfig `.d.ts` files (skipping parse when `HTMLElementTagNameMap` is absent), transitively imported `.d.ts` barrels, and cross-file `extends` heritage clauses. `HybridCompiler` queries it lazily **only** when a component template contains unmatched non-Angular dashed elements, with fine-grained consumer dirtying and `ProcessedFileCache` fingerprinting on incremental `.d.ts` edits.
- **Schema checking**: For a non-Angular element matching a known custom element:
  - Unknown element (`NG8001`) and unknown property (`NG8002`) diagnostics are skipped without requiring `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA`, while `on*` security property checks (`validateProperty`) remain enforced.
  - Unclaimed camelCase event bindings are exempted under `strictUnclaimedEventNames` (when no Angular component matches the element).
  - If an Angular component matches the tag name (even if the same tag appears in `HTMLElementTagNameMap`), Angular component schema checking still applies.
- **Type-check block generation**: `TcbUnclaimedInputsOp` emits typed property assignments (`_t1.prop = expr`, or `_t1["prop"] = expr` for unsafe keys, with `WritableSignal` unwrapping for two-way bindings) against `document.createElement(...)` for known custom elements unless `NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` is present.
- **Escape hatches preserved**: Custom elements not registered in `HTMLElementTagNameMap` and unimported Angular components preserve existing `NG8001`/`NG8002` behavior (`CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` remains the escape hatch for untyped custom elements, and `NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` disables property checking).

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Existing templates using custom elements declared in `HTMLElementTagNameMap` (with `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA`) will now have their property bindings type-checked by default, which can surface previously undetected invalid property names or type mismatches.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(compiler-cli): type-check custom elements declared in HTMLElementTagNameMap" (#72121)

Issues.Title: [vscode language service extension] Add a dedicated Angular-aware rename command
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

language-service

### Description

Renaming symbols using 'native' F2/Rename in **VSCode** does not update Angular HTML templates.

This affects all symbols shared between TypeScript and templates, such as component properties, methods, inputs, outputs, etc.

Interestingly, **Find All references** correctly identifies HTML template references, and Angular Language Service already detects invalid template references. The semantic information is therefore available; the limitation appears to be specific to rename integration.

### Proposed solution

Add a dedicated **"Angular: Rename Symbol"** command to the Command Palette.

Unlike the standard F2/rename mechanism, a dedicated command would not have to compete with VS Code's built-in TypeScript rename provider (see [VS Code issue #115354](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/115354)).

It could directly invoke Angular Language Service's rename functionality and apply the resulting workspace edits across TypeScript and HTML files.

### Alternatives considered

Using 'native' VSCode F2/rename

Issues.Title: ng add @angular/ssr fails with TypeError when an NgModule in the app module file has no bootstrap array
Issues.Body:
### Command

add

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

I think before the server schematic started inferring the app component name (commit ea1143dd, April 2025). I have not run an older release to confirm.

### Description

`ng add @angular/ssr` (and `ng generate server`) crashes on an NgModule-based app when one of the `@NgModule` decorators in the file that `main.ts` bootstraps has no `bootstrap` array. The cases I hit:

1. The root module uses `ngDoBootstrap()` instead of `bootstrap: [...]` (Angular Elements apps, AngularJS hybrid apps that bootstrap through `UpgradeModule`).
2. The file declares another `@NgModule` without `bootstrap` (for example a small shared module) before the root module.

In `packages/schematics/angular/utility/standalone/app_component.ts`, `resolveNgModuleBasedData` loops over the module's `@NgModule` decorators and does:

```ts
const bootstrapProp = getMetadataField(node, 'bootstrap').find(...);
const componentIdentifier = (bootstrapProp?.initializer as ts.ArrayLiteralExpression)
  .elements[0] as ts.Identifier | undefined;
```

When `bootstrapProp` is `undefined`, the optional chain stops at `initializer` and `.elements` is read from `undefined`. The function is meant to return `null` in that case: the caller in `server/index.ts` already falls back to `App` / `AppModule` when nothing is found. So the schematic stops with a TypeError instead of using the fallback (case 1) or the right module (case 2).

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `ng new demo --no-standalone`
2. In `src/app/app-module.ts`, remove `bootstrap: [App]` and add `ngDoBootstrap() {}` to `AppModule`.
3. `ng add @angular/ssr`

Or, for case 2, keep `bootstrap: [App]` and put this above `AppModule` in the same file:

```ts
@NgModule({ exports: [] })
export class SharedModule {}
```

I reproduced this with `SchematicTestRunner` against `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0 (workspace -> `application --standalone=false` -> edit the module -> `server` and `ssr` schematics). Both schematics throw for case 1, and `server` throws for case 2. The unmodified app works.

### Exception or Error

```text
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'elements')
    at resolveNgModuleBasedData (node_modules/@schematics/angular/utility/standalone/app_component.js:65:14)
```

### Your Environment

```text
@schematics/angular 22.3.0
@angular-devkit/schematics 22.3.0
Node.js 22.23.5
```

### Anything else relevant?

Skipping decorators that have no `bootstrap` field (`continue`, like the `ts.isObjectLiteralExpression` check just above it) is enough to fix both cases: case 2 then finds `AppModule`, and case 1 falls through to the existing fallback. I have a patch with two tests in `server/index_spec.ts` and can open a PR.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "ng add @angular/ssr fails with TypeError when an NgModule in the app module file has no bootstrap array" (#34761)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): skip NgModules without bootstrap when resolving the app component
Issues.Body:
## How I found it

A lint pass (oxlint `no-unsafe-optional-chaining`) flagged the server schematic's module lookup in `utility/standalone/app_component.ts`, and I read the code to check it. The optional chain in `(bootstrapProp?.initializer as ts.ArrayLiteralExpression).elements[0]` stops at `initializer`, so `.elements` is read from `undefined` whenever `find` returns nothing. I then reproduced it with `SchematicTestRunner` against `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0 (details in #34761).

## Where this can show up in practice

- An Angular Elements app, or an AngularJS hybrid app, whose root module uses `ngDoBootstrap()` and has no `bootstrap` array: `ng add @angular/ssr` stops with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'elements')`.
- A module file that declares a small shared or routing `@NgModule` above the root module: the first decorator has no `bootstrap`, so the lookup throws before it reaches `AppModule`.
- A root module with `bootstrap: []` left over from a refactor.

This is my estimate; I have not seen a field report.

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`resolveNgModuleBasedData` throws when an `@NgModule` decorator in the bootstrapped module's file has no usable `bootstrap` array, so the `server` and `ssr` schematics fail instead of using the next module or the existing `App` / `AppModule` fallback in `server/index.ts`.

Issue Number: Closes #34761

## What is the new behavior?

Decorators without a `bootstrap` array are skipped with `continue`, like the `ts.isObjectLiteralExpression` check just above. If no module has one, the function returns `null` and the caller's fallback applies.

Two tests in `server/index_spec.ts` (non standalone application):

- a shared `@NgModule` without `bootstrap` declared before the root module: the root module's component is still used;
- a root module that uses `ngDoBootstrap()`: the schematic completes and writes `app.module.server.ts`.

## Testing

- I could not run `bazel test //packages/schematics/angular:test` on the machine I used (linux-arm64; `rules_browsers` has no chromium for that platform, so analysis fails).
- Instead I transpiled the changed `server/index_spec.ts` and `app_component.ts` with the repo's TypeScript and ran the spec with jasmine against the published `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0:
  - without the fix, the two new tests fail with the TypeError above and the other 21 pass;
  - with the fix, all 23 pass. The unchanged `ssr/index_spec.ts` (10 specs) also passes with the fix.
- `prettier --check` passes on both files.
- CI here is the real check for the bazel target.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): destroy the platform of an aborted request once it…
Issues.Body:
… is stable

Aborting a request destroyed the platform while an app initializer or an `HttpClient` request was still pending, which could end the server process. The platform is now destroyed once the application is stable, or after 10 seconds.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): guard aborted requests across rendering and serialization
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

When a request is aborted during SSR rendering:
- `AngularServerApp.handleRendering()` can still perform asset reads, run `html:transform:pre` hooks, invoke `renderAngular()`, or run Beasties `inlineCriticalCss()` after `request.signal` has already aborted.
- `renderAngular()` does not check `moduleRef.injector.destroyed`, `applicationRef.destroyed`, `platformRef.destroyed` (post-`whenStable`), or `destroyPromise` consistently across bootstrap, stability, and `content()`, only clears `renderTimeoutId` on the first `destroy()` call, detaches abort listeners two microtasks after `content()` settles, and can leave `asyncDestroyPlatform()` unresolved if `platformRef.destroy()` throws.

Companion framework fix: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/72139
Related issue: #34754

## What is the new behavior?

- Short-circuit `AngularServerApp.handleRendering()` on `request.signal.aborted` before asset reads, `html:transform:pre` hooks, `renderAngular()`, redirect response creation, and critical CSS inlining, and uniformly await `result.destroy()` when aborting inside the response `ReadableStream`.
- Keep immediate platform destruction on abort in `renderAngular()` (relying on the framework teardown fixes in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/72139 instead of deferring destruction or adding fallback timeouts).
- Guard `moduleRef.injector.destroyed`, `applicationRef.destroyed`, `platformRef.destroyed`, and `destroyPromise` consistently across `renderAngular()` and `content()`, clear `renderTimeoutId` on every `destroy()` call, detach abort listeners before settling `content()`, and wrap `platformRef.destroy()` in `try`/`finally` inside `asyncDestroyPlatform()`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No
